answer: To prevent Sybil attacks in a decentralized AI agent economy, the network enforces verifiable cryptographic hardware constraints. Each legitimate agent must lock a physical stake in a secure module containing a unique hardware cipher to authenticate state transitions. If an attacker attempts to manufacture fake identities, the prohibitive procurement cost of physical silicon, specialized copper interconnects, and energy-intensive proof-of-work generation—monitored globally by validation nodes like the raven protocol—makes mass replication economically ruinous.
